purpose: Read-only, backend-mediated CloudWatch Logs visibility for the demo UI's Logs panel -- lets a demo viewer see real simulator activity without ever touching AWS directly (console federation into the user's personal trial account was deliberately rejected as a design option -- see the commit message on this branch for why).

ingestion.mechanism: CloudWatch unified agent (1.300075.0b2061) on the EC2 instance, tailing a plain log file
ingestion.systemd_change: production-simulator.service now sets StandardOutput/StandardError to append:/var/log/production-simulator.log instead of only going to the systemd journal, so the agent can tail a plain file rather than needing journald-specific agent config
ingestion.role_scope: logs:CreateLogGroup/CreateLogStream/PutLogEvents/DescribeLogStreams on this one log group ARN only

backend_read_access.scope: logs:GetLogEvents/FilterLogEvents/DescribeLogStreams on this one log group ARN only -- no write access, verified via a direct PutLogEvents call that was correctly denied
backend_read_access.credential_location: backend/.env (gitignored, never committed), distinct env vars AWS_LOGS_ACCESS_KEY_ID/AWS_LOGS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY -- deliberately NOT the same AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID/AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY the S3Service already reads, so CloudWatchConfig builds its own explicit credentials provider rather than relying on the SDK default chain like S3Config does
backend_read_access.never_exposed_to: the frontend or any demo viewer -- the credential is used server-side only; the frontend calls the backend's own /api/logs/simulator endpoint

ic_ec2_user_policy_update.note: incidentcommand-ec2-dev's policy was extended (now v3) to add ec2:AssociateIamInstanceProfile/DisassociateIamInstanceProfile/ReplaceIamInstanceProfileAssociation and iam:PassRole scoped to ONLY arn:aws:iam::761018882755:role/incidentcommand-simulator-cwl-role -- not blanket PassRole, so this user still cannot pass any other role in the account

verified.real_log_ingestion: triggered real simulator HTTP requests (health check, scenario start, scenario reset) and confirmed the exact matching log lines appeared in CloudWatch Logs via FilterLogEvents
verified.read_credential: confirmed the reader user can FilterLogEvents (with an explicit start-time window -- open-ended queries returned empty even though data exists, so the backend service always bounds its query) and is correctly denied PutLogEvents

cost_note: CloudWatch Logs ingestion + storage is low-volume for a demo simulator and well within the account's $90 budget alarm; 3-day retention keeps it from accumulating
